title: Keystone packs: per-domain calibration sampling protocol for FP8/INT8 validation
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: define and produce 'keystone' calibration packs — compact, per-domain datasets optimized for model calibration and accuracy validation when building FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles. Keystone packs are intended to be small (1k–10k prompts depending on domain), reproducible, and representative of production distribution slices so that calibration runs and post-quantization accuracy gates are fast and predictive of real-world regressions.

Scope: sampling protocol, metadata schema for sampled prompts, holdout/validation splits, automatic sensitivity scoring for prompts, and recommended pack sizes per domain. This ticket covers design, implementation scripts (sampling + metadata export), and a smoke validation harness that runs quantize->calibrate->eval on the keystone packs for a target model family (redwood-v1-like) on FP8 and INT8 profiles.
acceptance_criteria: Specification of per-domain keystone pack schema (fields: prompt_id, domain_tag, cluster_id, seq_length, frequency, recency_score, sensitivity_score, artifact_links)
Sampling tool that generates keystone packs for a domain given: domain label, target_size, sensitivity_threshold, recency_weight config
Automated calibration pipeline: run quantize profiles (FP8/INT8) -> calibrate on pack -> evaluate on holdout; outputs: EM/ROUGE-L/per-token-logit-shift and per-domain accuracy delta report

Baseline vs quantized accuracy delta documented for 5 pilot domains (ui-automation, search, finance, support-chat, summarization) with target max accuracy drop <= 2% absolute for FP8 and <= 1% for INT8 for high-sensitivity domains
Pack export artifact uploaded to Drive + manifest with reproducible seed and sampling config
Integration test in CI that verifies sampling tool produces identical pack when given same seed and dataset snapshot
comments: 2026-02-20 Ava Martinez: Kickoff — initial problem statement. We need small, high-signal calibration sets that map to production prompt slices. Current large calibration sets are expensive to iterate and sometimes miss high-sensitivity prompt families. Goal is to reduce calibration cycle from hours to ~20–30 minutes for nightly runs.

2026-02-24 Liam Chen: Proposed sampling algorithm: compute per-prompt sensitivity score by running baseline vs half-precision simulated quantization (pseudo-quant using weight perturbations) and measuring logit-shift and token-level KL. Use score to prioritize examples during pack construction. Combine with frequency and recency weights: w = alpha * normalized_sensitivity + beta * log(1+frequency) + gamma * recency_decay. Default alpha=0.6, beta=0.25, gamma=0.15.

2026-03-02 Sofia Patel (Applied ML): Trade-offs: sensitivity estimation is costly; for initial pass we can use a proxy sensitivity computed from influence fingerprints (embedding-distance to recent failing prompts) and token-id-frequency variance to approximate which prompts amplify quantization error. Will prototype both approaches and compare correlation with full sim sensitivity.

2026-03-05 Engineering review: Decided to stratify by cluster (semantic prompt clusters) and by sequence length buckets (<=64, 65-256, >256). Each pack will sample proportionally from clusters but reweight by sensitivity so rare but high-sensitivity clusters are upsampled. Also agreed on a mandatory 10% held-out validation split (stratified by cluster) for post-quantize accuracy checks.

2026-03-09 PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/4823 — sampling-tool + pack-manifest export. Includes reproducible-seed support and ability to ingest a 'production-snapshot' parquet with prompt metadata. CI smoke run added (simulated quantize + evaluate).

2026-03-12 Liam Chen: Pilot results (finance domain, pack size=2,000): sensitivity-weighted sampling reduced worst-case per-prompt logit-shift 95th percentile by ~18% vs random stratified sampling. FP8 calibration on pack resulted in mean token-level perplexity change +0.8%, overall QA F1 drop 0.9% — within target. Need more domains to confirm.

Actions: 1) Run pilot for remaining 4 domains, 2) finalize pack-size recommendations per domain, 3) add automatic thresholding to cap upsampling for very low-frequency clusters, 4) schedule design review for pack manifest schema and naming conventions.
